articles.title: Sense and Sensibility review – Daisy Edgar-Jones leads sober-minded next-gen do-over of Austen romcom
articles.summary: With Edgar-Jones and Esmé Creed-Miles as the Dashwood sisters, this fresh take on a beloved classic is not to be confused with Ang Lee’s. There’s no reason for anyone working on a new adaptation of Jane Austen’s Sense and Sensibility to be intimidated by the celebrated 1995 movie by director Ang…
body: The sisters at the heart of the story, Elinor and Marianne Dashwood, played in 1995 by Emma Thompson and Kate Winslet, are now played by Daisy Edgar-Jones and Esmé Creed-Miles, and frankly don’t look and sound much like the sisters we thought we knew. They look like young women who knew each other reasonably well at uni and are now in a flatshare in London. It is a story of financial and romantic crisis. Mrs Dashwood and her three daughters, having happily occupied a handsome Sussex estate, are forced to move to humble Barton Cottage in Devon when Mrs Dashwood’s stepson John Dashwood inherits their property and effectively evicted them.

Before this can happen, Elinor meets and falls for young Edward Ferrars, a shy and decent young man of a well-to-do family, reticently portrayed by George MacKay. Here, in fact, it should be said that Diana Reid’s script and Georgia Oakley’s direction put into valuably sharper focus something left unstressed in 1995: that Mrs Dashwood (Caitríona Balfe) is pointedly insisting on moving away to the west country rather than endure the indignity of her daughter seeming to be a gold-digger.

articles.title: SCAD Savannah Film Festival to Open With ‘A Talent for Murder’ and Legend of Entertainment Honor for Helen Mirren
articles.summary: The SCAD Savannah Film Festival will open its 29th edition with the Anton Corbijn thriller “A Talent for Murder” and will honor Helen Mirren with its Legend of Entertainment Award.
body: Distributed by Bleecker Street and LD Entertainment, “A Talent for Murder” follows a mysterious young man (Alden Ehrenreich) dispatched by a New York publisher to Switzerland, where he must persuade a renowned author (Mirren) to write one final installment of a legendary thriller anthology.

More than 74,000 people attend the eight-day festival each year, which packs SCAD’s historic theaters and studio spaces with competition titles, features, documentaries, shorts, animation, panels and workshops. Variety will once again be partnering with the festival for its annual Pixels and Pencils panel, which honors directors of animated feature films, and 10 Artisans to Watch, recognizing up and coming craftspeople in the industry.

For Mirren, the tribute lands as one of the most decorated careers in the business. The actress won the Academy Award for best actress for “The Queen” and drew Oscar nominations for “The Madness of King George,” “Gosford Park” and “The Last Station.” She has also collected a Tony, four Emmys and multiple BAFTA, Golden Globe and Screen Actors Guild honors across film, television and the stage.

articles.title: Warner Chappell Co-Chair/COO Carianne Marshall to Step Down From Post
articles.summary: Warner Music Group has announced that Carianne Marshall will transition out of her role as co-chair and chief operating officer of Warner Chappell Music, the company’s publishing division, at the end of this month, “as the company streamlines its leadership structure,” the announcement reads.
body: Marshall joined Warner Chappell in June of 2018 following the sale of Songs music publishing — the company that rose to success with the Weeknd, Lorde and others, where she was a partner — and has co-led the publisher alongside Moot since April 2019.
She played a key role in Warner Chappell’s modernization of digital licensing, the introduction of its creative services department and multiple major signings.
The company’s key writers include Tom Petty, Grammy songwriter of the year Amy Allen, Kacey Musgraves, Raye, Gamble & Huff and others.

Warner Music CEO Robert Kyncl said: “Carianne has been instrumental in building Warner Chappell into the successful company it is today. She’s helped drive exceptional results that have set our songwriters and our business up for long-lasting success. Our talented team will build upon the incredible foundation she’s put in place. We thank her for her dedication, impact and wish her the very best in her next chapter.”

articles.title: American Film Market Partners With AMC A-List and B-List Movie Club to Offer Screenings to Frequent Moviegoers
articles.summary: The American Film Market is partnering with AMC to further engage both buyers and audiences, giving AMC A-List and B-List Movie Club members access to screenings and presentations from exhibiting companies.
body: Added Carrie Trotter, senioor vice president of marketing at AMC Theatres: “AMC A-List members are among the most passionate moviegoers in the industry, and we’re always looking for new ways to connect them with unique theatrical experiences. We’re excited to collaborate with AFM and engage communities like The B-List Movie Club to give movie fans access to special screenings, discover upcoming films, and experience content that isn’t typically available to general audiences.”
Brett Gaffney, founder of the B-List Movie Club, and vice president Jenna Webster said they are “honored and excited” to partner with the AFM.

“Moviegoing is and should always be community oriented, and The B-List Movie Club members are some of the most passionate movie fans around,” they said. “Inviting our members to the AFM will help filmmakers see how a real audience responds to a film and will provide valuable insight into the direction of a future theatrical release.”

articles.title: The Seasons review – Portuguese pastoral offers poetic excavation of myth and mapping
articles.summary: The rugged roads and lush vegetation of southern Portugal are showcased in this weaving-together of disparate threads of history and landscape. In a sea of doomsday ecological documentaries, Maureen Fazendeiro’s pastoral marvel is a sight for sore eyes.
body: The abundant use of tracking shots not only takes in the wondrous biodiversity of Alentejo but also facilitates a fluid movement between separate epochs. Observational scenes of green hills, boundless blue skies and roaming livestock are overlaid with narrated excerpts from second world war-era letters written by German archaeologists Georg and Vera Leisner. Credited with producing the first inventory of megalithic monuments in Alentejo, the pair imbues their wartime correspondence with the joy of discovery and the sadness of exile.

Elsewhere, history is preserved in oral tradition. One scene observes a circle of elders, in which a woman laments the rise of fascism and the fall of socialism in song, wistful melodies that reminds us of the years of António de Oliveira Salazar’s dictatorship. Another striking sequence takes a leap of imagination by re-staging a 17th-century myth. In weaving together these disparate threads of narrative, Fazendeiro’s sumptuous film offers an alternative form of geographical mapping, in which a landscape can be read like a text or a poem, to be preserved and passed on to future generations.

articles.title: Heart of the action: why organ couriers are cinema’s new heroes
articles.summary: Whether its a nod to frontline Covid heroes or a return to biology in a world of digital noise, there’s a rich vein of new films featuring organ deliveries, including Runner and the latest Resident Evil. Hollywood loves a ticking clock – especially when there’s a delivery involved.
body: Lately, however, Hollywood seems interested in a different kind of hero – not to mention a different kind of cargo. Forget your nuclear launch codes, stolen diamonds and mysterious briefcases, for human organs are the new MacGuffins du jour, and the medical professionals charged with getting them to the ICU have become unlikely action heroes.

Take Runner, directed by Scott Waugh, which stars Alan “Reacher” Ritchson as a delivery driver caught in a race against time, and Owen Wilson as an organ courier carrying a liver with a life-or-death deadline. “If she doesn’t get this today,” Wilson says of the girl awaiting the transplant, “she’s not going to make it.”

Co-writer Miles Hubley says he and writing partner Tommy White wanted “a device that wasn’t just about money”, adding: “Neither of us had ever seen a movie where the precious cargo everyone wants was a fragile, life-saving piece of tissue.”

Waugh agrees: an organ gives the film “emotional urgency”. “It’s the idea of a protagonist being driven not by revenge or saving the world, but simply by an obligation to deliver something on time,” he says. “You’ve got a deadline and someone whose life depends on you arriving.”

articles.title: London Fashion Week 2026: The five trends we'll see in spring
articles.summary: As London Fashion Week comes to a close, here are the biggest trends for your wardrobe.
body: This London Fashion Week has been about return and renewal - as two of Britain's biggest designers showcased their spring/summer 2027 designs.

The first was Alexander McQueen, which as a brand moved to London after 25 years of showing in Paris - something Laura Weir, CEO of the British Fashion Council, told the BBC was "quite a big deal for us".
Creative director Seán McGirr brought the brand back to its roots, with a runway of devil horns, lace corsets and chainmail skull dresses.

Mulberry was the second designer to make its big return, this time after a nine-year absence, with Christopher Kane's debut collection centring around the brand's Baywater bag, while going big on leather in the form of coats, skirts and loafers.

articles.title: Dunesday: will this be Barbenheimer on steroids – the biggest weekend of cinema ever?
articles.summary: Since the mammoth success of the films Barbie and Oppenheimer in 2023, Hollywood has taken to jointly marketing movies released on the same day – and December’s matchup of Dune: Part Three and Avengers: Doomsday could break all records. Name: Dunesday. Age: Nascent.
body: I’ve just arrived on this planet. Barbenheimer? The momentous day in July 2023 when Barbie and Oppenheimer were simultaneously released into cinemas worldwide.
And everyone picked sides? Or they saw both films on the same day, causing tonal whiplash from which they may still be recovering.

Fun times. And lucrative times, too. Barbie made $356m (£285m) worldwide on its opening weekend, while Oppenheimer shattered expectations by taking $180m. The £36m spent in UK cinemas that weekend made it the most successful since 2019, while it was the fourth-biggest box office weekend in the US ever.

So the Barbenheimer effect was real? Absolutely. For perhaps the first time, filmgoers en masse saw the dual releases of two blockbusters as complimentary, rather than a contest. Anyway, forget about Barbenheimer, because this December welcomes Dunesday, which will be Barbenheimer on steroids.

articles.title: CNN, MS NOW and Politico file lawsuit against Trump's White House ban
articles.summary: Major US networks later suspended White House TV coverage of Trump as he heads to New York for the UN summit.
body: CNN, Politico and MS NOW have sued the Trump administration after the three US media outlets were barred from the White House.

President Donald Trump announced the ban on Friday, accusing the organisations of writing "fiction or lies" about his team. The companies said their reporters were denied access to the building on Saturday.
In a joint statement on Monday, they said they were pursuing legal action to "defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports".
Major US TV networks later announced they would suspend their White House pooled coverage of Trump, leaving a potential gap as he heads to New York for the United Nations General Assembly.
